title: Lonely Pixel I
statement: `picture` is an `m x n` image whose cells are the characters `'B'` (a black pixel) and `'W'` (a white pixel). Call a black pixel at row `r` and column `c` **lonely** when it is the only `'B'` anywhere in row `r` and also the only `'B'` anywhere in column `c`. Return how many lonely black pixels the picture has.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking each black pixel by scanning its row and column works, but costs O(m·n·(m + n)). A pixel is lonely exactly when its row holds one `'B'` and its column holds one `'B'`, so it is enough to know how many black pixels each row and each column contains. One pass counts them; a second pass tests every black pixel against the counts.

## Approach

1. Make `rowCount` (one slot per row) and `colCount` (one slot per column), all zero.
2. First pass: for every `'B'` at `[r, c]`, add one to `rowCount[r]` and `colCount[c]`.
3. Second pass: for every `'B'` at `[r, c]`, if `rowCount[r] === 1` and `colCount[c] === 1`, add one to `lonely`.
4. Return `lonely`.

## Example 1, step by step

The black pixels sit at `[0,2]`, `[1,1]` and `[2,0]`. After the first pass `rowCount = [1, 1, 1]` and `colCount = [1, 1, 1]`. In the second pass each of the three black pixels finds a count of 1 in both its row and its column, so `lonely` becomes 3, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m·n): two passes over the picture.
- Space: O(m + n) for the two count arrays.

## Pitfalls

- Being alone in its row is not enough; the column must also have no other `'B'`.
- Test that the cell itself is `'B'` in the second pass: a white cell in a row and column that each hold one black pixel is not a lonely pixel.
- The cells are one-character strings, so compare with `'B'`, not a number or a boolean.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | the picture's height and width |
| `rowCount` | number of black pixels in each row |
| `colCount` | number of black pixels in each column |
| `r`, `c` | the current cell's row and column |
| `lonely` | how many lonely black pixels have been found |

narration.4: One black-pixel counter per row, all starting at zero.
narration.5: One black-pixel counter per column, all starting at zero.
narration.10: This row has one more black pixel.
narration.17: Second pass: visit every cell again, now that the counts are complete.
narration.19: A black pixel is lonely when its row and its column each hold exactly one black pixel, itself.
narration.24: Return the number of lonely black pixels.
